message:
Thanks for this, Mike. Your memory of my talk may be better than mine, since I delivered a couple of different versions (C&W, RSA) that summer.

The only thing I'd add is that one of the points I was raising was the relationship between Blizzard's decision to sell the CS and the idea of the "magic circle" of the game--the CS was the first in-game item to be sold for "real-world" money, and it caused no small amount of consternation among many of the WoW players. I do think there are some disciplinary/organizational implications there--academic organizations and disciplines have their own magic circles, too.

There's at least a blogpost in me about this waiting to get out, in part because I'm fascinated by the fact that a line can be drawn from a single slide in a Keynote deck to national media coverage of our field (even if I'm only tangentially responsible for that virality). And like Nels, I have a more complicated set of associations and contexts attached to the idea--I'm still sorting through them. But I really appreciate the background you provided here.

cgb
